display_name: Interpretation (Jersey) Law 1954 (L.17/1954): Articles 1 to 18 and the Schedule in all seven deposited versions
seat: The reader of an enactment: the individual who has to know what an enactment means for them, when it bound them, what may be done to them, and whether a notice reached them in time. Every exported question is phrased as that person would ask it, with inputs in facts that person could state.
source: Interpretation (Jersey) Law 1954 (L.17/1954), Official Consolidated Versions on jerseylaw.je, seven point-in-time texts retrieved 2026-10-27; terms in SOURCE-LICENSE.md (Open States Assembly Licence - Jersey v1.0)
versions_encoded: All seven deposited texts, each its own answer, chosen from a date by the vintage table in je54-vintage.l4. For a day from 28 March 2003 to 31 December 2018 only Article 1(5), Article 1(6) and the Schedule definitions of month and midnight are answered, labelled as inferred from the endnotes of the 2019 consolidation; every other provision refuses before 1 January 2019, and everything refuses before 28 March 2003.

scope.encoded: The title, long title and commencement note, Articles 1 to 18 and the Schedule (Part 1, the defined expressions; Part 2, the index) in each of the seven texts, including the paragraphs that exist in some texts only (Articles 1(2), 1(5), 1(6), 6, 11(3), 11(4), 16 and 17 in V1; Article 11A from V2a; the Article 8 limbs for a bank, a limited liability company and an administration order; the definitions of child and parent from V2e); 151 coverage rows over 855 paragraph lines, in NOTES.md section 4. Six forks, I1 to I6, each with a callable alternative and a test (NOTES.md section 6); fork I7 is considered and not registered. 43 exported questions in the reader's words.
scope.not_encoded: The Legislation (Jersey) Law 2021 (its rule for the commencement of enactments made on or after 28 September 2021 is a refusal that names it); the contents of the other enactments the Law mentions (inputs); any text of the Law before 1 January 2019 beyond the four inferred items; the counting of days, weeks, years or calendar months (the Law has no rule and no function does it); geometry for Article 15. The endnotes are evidence, not provisions, and have no coverage row.

check: check.sh (several minutes; needs the l4 binary named by l4_binary_sha256; L4 names the binary, L4_TARGET defaults to unstable)

checks.note: check.sh output pasted in NOTES.md section 9. A green run says nothing about whether a domain expert agrees with any reading, and srcrefs.py does not prove that a quoted line is the paragraph its @ref names (NOTES.md F2).

assertions_note: Satisfied assertions in the check.sh run of 2026-10-28, 32 modules: 1252 in the encoder's own tests modules and 520 in the three independent-pass modules (je54-tests-independent-1 to -3); no assertion fails on purpose and none is refused on purpose.
not_reviewed: No domain expert (a Jersey lawyer, or anyone who knows how Jersey courts and drafters read the Interpretation Law) has read any module of this encoding against the Law. The encoder checked its own modules against the deposited texts and wrote its tests with expected values taken from the source; an independent test pass by another session was run and its 14 findings are triaged in NOTES.md section 10.3 (33 of the encoder's own expected values were changed after it). Nothing here is verified beyond that, and nothing here is legal advice.
encoder_detail: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), one subagent session in October 2026 working to BRIEF.md; model, reading and commands are recorded in NOTES.md section 11.

independent_pass.run_by: the team lead, a fresh Claude Sonnet 5.5 session that decided its scenarios from the text before opening the encoding (its decisions.md is not deposited)
independent_pass.notes: NOTES.md section 10.3; the answers are one reader's, assumed, not ruled
